scope: Artificial intelligence in health care for year 1-2 students of medicine, pharmacy, physical therapy and the health sciences: clinical grounding, computational rigour, assessment realism and medicolegal accuracy.
criteria: Clinical terminology is exact, e.g. sensitivity in screening versus specificity in confirmatory testing.
Clinical workflows reflect real care settings: EHR integration, PACS/DICOM handoffs, laboratory information systems.
Architectures are defined precisely: CNNs for spatial grids, ViTs for patch attention, U-Net for segmentation.
Metric choice fits the claim: AUROC versus AUPRC under class imbalance, Dice for segmentation, calibration for risk.
Training, validation and external test sets are kept apart and leakage risks are stated.
CADe, CADx and CADt are distinguished under SaMD guidance.
Liability is anchored in named doctrines: standard of care, learned intermediary, vicarious liability.
MCQ stems are realistic scenarios; distractors are plausible mimics; rationales teach the mechanism.
Every chapter is readable by all four professions without prior clinical training.
exclusions: Specialist procedures dropped by the design (e.g. TAVR planning, IVUS/OCT, EVAR) are not re-requested.
evidence_expectations: Quote the exact text and give file and line for every finding.
Give replacement text, not only a critique.
Cite a verifiable source for any corrected number, trial or regulation.
